title: Airport greetings and George Masso, 'Son of Chief'
summary: Moore tells of people calling out to him at airports and of dubbing trombonist George Masso 'Son of Chief' after a Lanin job.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: It becomes a small world in the world of musicians sometimes.

Sometimes I go through the airport and I hear somebody hollering, 'Hey, Chief,' and I remember the 'Loch Lomond' girl?---turn around and there was Maxie Sullivan -/ 'Hey, Chief, where ya going?' And I'd tell them where I was going, 'Where you going yourself?' They're going here and there. Another guy hollers at me at the airport, comedian, George Kirby. They used to all holler at me at the airport. Invariably when I'd walk into the airport, some guy would run up to me and say, some guy says to say hello to you, he's on his way to such and such a place and it was someone I knew years back.
Passed the word on, second or third hand.
Sometimes when I'm in bed I think of things that happened to me and I start laughing. This happened just lately when I was with Lester Lanin. We played a place in Galveston and on that same

bandstand I heard so much about, George Masso, he's a beautiful, beautiful trombone player and he played, I played and we had a wonderful time, and he was a beautiful trombone player; and when we were on the plane coming back from Galveston before we got into the airport at LaGuardia, I walked over to George Masso and said, 'George, from now on you're one of my favorite trombone players. You played so great tonight' He thanked me for it and then I said, George, from now on you'll be called the 'Son of Chief,' and he laughed and laughed. He said, 'Quite an honor to be called 'Son of Chief.'
